answers.rationale: Job J1 uses service_code TOW with 4 billed_hours on 2024-06-03 (jobs.csv). Service conditions §1 apply the rate_card TOW row at 240 per hour. Vessel V-NORTH has only this job that day, so no overtime adjustment under §2 (under 8 hours).
Job J4 is coded ASST (jobs.csv). Service conditions §4 require billing ASST jobs at the ESCORT rate_card row, not the ASST row. ESCORT is 180 per hour (rate_card.csv).
Service conditions §5 state that blank billed_hours is not an established billable quantity. Only job J6 has a blank billed_hours field in jobs.csv; all other jobs have a numeric value.

Job J2 is TOW with 9 billed_hours for vessel V-BAY on 2024-06-03 (jobs.csv). Base rate is 240/hr (rate_card.csv). Service conditions §2: hours beyond 8 in one calendar day for a single vessel are charged at 1.5× for those extra hours only. V-BAY has no other jobs that day, so 8×240 + 1×(240×1.5) = 1920 + 360 = 2280.

Service conditions §6 state fuel surcharges are published in a separate circular and that this excerpt does not contain a fuel schedule. No fuel surcharge schedule is present in the sources folder, so no fuel surcharge amount for job J3 can be established.

Job J7 is a TOW at berth B12 from 20:00–21:30 on 2024-06-05 (jobs.csv), which is after 18:00. Berth notice states commercial towing at B12 after 18:00 is permitted only for a documented emergency, but explicitly notes that no emergency log is attached and documentation is not included in the packet. The job comment ('after hours') does not constitute documented emergency authorization.
